original_value: Attribute-Based Encryption (ABE) must provide an efficient revocation mechanism since a user’s private key can be compromised or expired over time. The existing revocable ABE schemes have the drawbacks of heavy computational costs on key updates and encryption operations, which make the entities for performing these operations a possible bottleneck in practice applications. In this paper, we propose an efficient Ciphertext-Policy Attribute-Based Online/Offline Encryption with user Revocation (R-CP-ABOOE). We integrate the subset difference method with ciphertext-policy ABE to significantly improve key-update efficiency on the side of the trusted party from O(rlog⁡(N/r)) to O(r), where N is the number of users and r is the number of revoked users. To reduce the encryption burden for mobile devices, we use the online/offline technology to shift the majority of encryption work to the offline phase, and then mobile devices only need to execute a few simple computations to create a ciphertext. In addition, we exploit a novel trick to prove its selective security under the q-type assumption. Performance analysis shows that our scheme greatly improves the key-update efficiency for the trusted party and the encryption efficiency for mobile devices.

result.paraphrase: Attribute-Based Encryption (ABE) needs an efficient revocation mechanism because a user’s private key may be compromised or expire over time. Existing revocable ABE schemes suffer from high computational overhead in key updates and encryption, making the parties that perform these tasks potential bottlenecks in practical applications. In this paper, we present an efficient Ciphertext-Policy Attribute-Based Online/Offline Encryption with User Revocation (R-CP-ABOOE). By combining the subset difference method with ciphertext-policy ABE, we greatly improve the trusted party’s key-update efficiency from O(rlog⁡(N/r)) to O(r), where N is the number of users and r is the number of revoked users. To lessen the encryption load on mobile devices, we apply online/offline techniques that move most encryption work to the offline phase, so mobile devices need only perform a few simple computations to produce a ciphertext. We also use a novel trick to prove selective security under the q-type assumption. Performance analysis indicates that our scheme substantially improves key-update efficiency for the trusted party and encryption efficiency for mobile devices.
